name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement refused its run
message: A scheduled statement on {{host.name}} refused its run, or could not run at all (broken): its slot is marked refused and the next runs as due, so the work of this one is not done. The server's log names the statement, the slot, the status and why, with the run's request_id; `statements` (or GET /_schema) shows its `last` mark. A guard unmet (412) is the statement saying so; a broken one (409) is mended by `create or replace statement`.

name: fennecdb: a scheduled run's outcome is unknown
message: A scheduled statement's run on {{host.name}} landed as its tenant's lease lapsed, or its fsync failed: whether the file holds its writes and its slot's mark -- on a tenant node, whether the tenant's next primary does -- is unknown, as a client's write would be answered 500. Where they were lost the slot runs again wherever the file is written next; where they were kept it ran once. The server's log names the statement and the slot with the run's request_id. A failed fsync stops the database's writes until it is opened again: check the disk. A lapsed lease: check the node's link to its router.

name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement's slot is held back
message: A scheduled statement's slot on {{host.name}} was refused by the state of its database -- a tenant at its quota (507), a lapsed lease, a storage error -- and is held: tried again as the data or the limit changes, or after a backoff of a minute doubling to fifteen. Nothing of it is lost while it is held, but nothing of it is done, and the next slot passes over it. `statements` shows `held` with the status and since when; the log names the first refusal.

name: fennecdb: a scheduled statement's mark is ahead of the clock
message: A scheduled statement's last mark on {{host.name}} stands ahead of the server's clock: the clock was stepped back behind a run, or a clock that was ahead ran it. Within an hour its slots wait for the clock to pass the mark; further ahead the schedule goes on from the clock and the slots the wrong clock ran run again as they come. Check the host's NTP. The audit log's `clock` line names the statement, the mark and the clock.

name: fennecdb: scheduled statements run late
message: Scheduled runs on {{host.name}} began more than two minutes past their slots (p99): a node's tenants due at one instant run one at a time, each behind the runs before it, and a restart runs a missed slot late. Lateness is no fault in itself -- `slot()` names the slot a run was for -- but a node always this late wants its tenants' schedules spread or fewer tenants.

name: fennecdb: webhook events do not verify
message: Events sent to {{host.name}}'s hooks were refused before their signature verified ({{check.name}}), each answered the one 401 that names no check. `signature`: a secret rotated at the sender and not here -- set the new one beside the old (a hooks file's second secret file, or PUT /_shard/tenants/<t>/hooks/<name> with both) -- or someone forging events. `hook`: a sender pointed at a hook this server does not hold, or a tenant whose secret was never set (a restore takes none back). `stale`: the sender's clock, or this host's, is off by more than the hook's tolerance -- check NTP. `scheme`, `header`: the sender is not the scheme the hook names. `size`: an event past the hook's ceiling (`max-body`). The server's log and the audit's `refused` line name the hook, the sender's address and the check under each request's id; a sender's own delivery log shows the 401s.

name: fennecdb: a webhook event was refused by a statement
message: Verified webhook events on {{host.name}} were refused by what they came to: a statement's guard (412), a parameter missing or of another type (400), an id or unique value held (409), a statement broken or no statement taking the hook (409). The sender keeps each and sends it again -- Stripe for three days, Svix for about 28 hours, GitHub not at all -- so a guard waiting for its row is the queue working; a statement that can never take an event is not. The server's log names the hook, the event's key, the status and the engine's words; `/_stats/statements` counts each statement as `hook <name>`, its errors the events it refused. Mend the statement with `create or replace statement` and the sender's retries are taken.

name: fennecdb: webhook events are held back
message: Verified webhook events on {{host.name}} were told to come back by the state they met -- a tenant at its quota (507) or its rate (429), a move's freeze or a lapsed lease (503), a storage error (500), no standby holding the event in time (503) -- or landed as a lease lapsed, their outcome unknown (500). Nothing is lost while the sender retries, and a retry of one that landed is answered from its key; but nothing is taken either. The server's log names each with its status; raise the quota, check the disk, the standby's stream (`fennec_replica_behind`) or the node's lease.

name: fennecdb: a tenant's copy lacks its hook secrets
message: The router on {{host.name}} counts tenants a copy of which -- a pair's standby, a `--replicas` copy -- lacks the version of the tenant's hook secrets its directory records: a failover onto that copy would answer the tenant's senders 401 until the secret is set again. The router's repair copies the set from a copy holding it on its next look; GET /_shard/tenants/<t>/hooks names the copy `behind`. If it stays, the copy's node is down or refuses the set: PUT the hook again once it is back.
